topic: The certification trap: why Security+ alone won't land you the job
post_text:
I spent 6 months grinding for Security+ thinking it was the golden ticket to a junior analyst role.

Passed it. Still got rejected from 40+ jobs.

Then a mentor told me something that changed everything: "Certifications open doors. Projects open minds."

I pivoted. Started building actual security work—not just studying for exams. Set up a home lab, documented a malware analysis, created a practical writeup on a real CVE. Published it on GitHub. Showed it in interviews.

First interview with the portfolio included? Three offers in two weeks.

Here's what I learned:

✓ Employers see hundreds of Security+ holders
✓ They see maybe five who can DEMONSTRATE what they know
✓ Certifications prove you studied material
✓ Projects prove you can actually do the work

If you're studying for a cert right now—great. Do it. But don't stop there. Build something. Break something safely. Document it. Show it off.

Your first security job isn't won on a test score. It's won by showing you're dangerous enough to be useful, and safe enough to trust.

What's holding you back from building your first security project? Is it technical gaps, time, or just not knowing where to start?
